# HDFC Bank Limited

<!-- Generated by `make client-docs`. Do not edit inside the markers. -->

Researched 2026-09-29 · status **complete**

HDFC Bank Limited runs its CSR programme under the brand 'Parivartan' across six focus areas (rural development, promotion of education, skill training & livelihood enhancement, healthcare & hygiene, financial literacy & inclusion, natural resource management). HDFC Bank's own decade CSR report (FY2024-25) discloses total pan-India CSR spend of ₹1,068.03 crore for FY2024-25 and 10.56 crore cumulative lives impacted, but does NOT break spend down by state. Seven Northeast state-level 'Towards A Better Tomorrow' booklets (March 2025) were located and read for Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Sikkim, Tripura, and a combined Nagaland & Manipur report, plus Arunachal Pradesh — confirming multiple named projects, districts, partner NGOs and beneficiary/impact counts in each state, but none of these state booklets disclose rupee spend figures per project or per state; only physical/beneficiary impact metrics (lives impacted, farmers supported, villages covered, schools built, etc.) are reported. Northeast India is not named anywhere as a distinct strategic priority geography; it is covered as part of Parivartan's stated pan-India presence in '28 States and 8 Union Territories', alongside general commitments to 'interior tribal regions, border villages, aspirational districts... hilly areas, deserts, and forests.' The project types found in the Northeast (HRDP/FDP rural development, smart schools, solar lighting, SHG/livelihood enterprises, healthcare infrastructure upgrades) mirror the same templates used nationally (e.g., in Odisha, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh stories in the decade report), indicating Northeast activity is a standard instance of the pan-India model rather than a bespoke regional programme. csrbox.org and Facebook links were HELD per registry rules and skipped as instructed; a Telegraph India article and an HDFC Bank press release page returned unreadable/403 content and could not be used as corroboration.

Website: https://v.hdfc.bank.in/csr/index.html

## Programmes

- **Parivartan delivery models**: Holistic Rural Development Programme (HRDP, cluster ~15 villages, 36-48 months) and Focused Development Programme (FDP, cluster ~25 villages, 2-48 months)
  > HRDP adopts a comprehensive approach to sustainable development by integrating interventions across all 6 focus areas... Under FDP, the bank carries out specific interventions under any one or two of the key focus areas in a targeted geographical area.
  <sub>HDFC Bank Parivartan Assam State Report, March 2025 · https://v.hdfc.bank.in/content/dam/hdfc-aem-microsites/csr/pdfs/state-report/CSR_Booklet_Assam_March2025.pdf · confidence high</sub>
- **Parivartan focus areas (pillars)**: Rural development; skill training & livelihood enhancement; promotion of education; healthcare & hygiene; financial literacy & inclusion; natural resource management
  > Parivartan has been a catalyst in making a difference in the lives of people through its interventions in the areas of rural development, education, skill development and livelihood enhancement, healthcare & hygiene and financial literacy.
  <sub>HDFC Bank CSR site · https://v.hdfc.bank.in/csr/index.html · confidence high</sub>
- **Arunachal Pradesh — HRDP rural livelihoods, Lohit district** (FY2024-25): 3,500+ farmers; partners Citizens Foundation and People to People Help Foundation
  > HDFC Bank Parivartan, in partnership with Citizens Foundation and People to People Help Foundation, is enhancing rural livelihoods through its Holistic Rural Development Programme (HRDP). The initiative supports 3,500+ farmers.
  <sub>HDFC Bank Parivartan Arunachal Pradesh State Report, March 2025 · https://v.hdfc.bank.in/content/dam/hdfc-aem-microsites/csr/pdfs/state-report/CSR_Booklet_ArunachalPradesh_March2025.pdf · confidence high</sub>
- **Arunachal Pradesh — healthcare infrastructure upgrade** (FY2024-25): 2 District Hospitals, 2 CHCs with maternity wards, 9 PHCs/CHCs upgraded across Lohit, Lower Dibang Valley, Papum Pare districts
